pass_summary: All five tasks are implemented as planned: the new headers are parsed and printed, orca_dispatch passes `repo` through to a `--repo path:<realpath> --no-parent` create (with a repo_not_registered hint and a list-based fallback instead of a lookup by name), and the audit follows Location with all three foreign findings and checks review evidence beside the Location file. The prose in both targets uses the real worktree_* schemas (worktree_create base_branch/project, worktree_abandon project, worktree_ensure project/base). The review found no blocking issues, only edge cases.

issues.title: A relative Location after the merge is resolved against Repo's main checkout, but the merge may land in a linked worktree
issues.description: src/spec/master-audit-foreign.ts resolveForeignChild: a relative `Location: docs/plans/<file>` is resolved with resolve(repo, location), where repo is the resolved `Repo:` (normally the main checkout). worktree_sync merges in the checkout that holds the base branch when one exists. If that is a linked worktree and the main checkout is on another branch, the merged copy is not at <Repo>/docs/plans/<file>, so the audit raises a false foreign-location-missing (or reads a stale copy). The prose F4 step (both targets) does not mention this case.
issues.suggested_fix: In the F4 step of targets/*/spec-master-execute, say that a relative Location is valid only once the base branch's checkout at `Repo:` contains the merge. Otherwise keep the absolute Location of the checkout where the merge landed (worktree_sync reports `Merged in:`). Or document this limitation in master-audit-foreign.ts.

issues.title: A relative Repo: resolves against the nearest .git, which is a linked/Orca worktree root when the coordinator runs in one
issues.description: src/spec/master-audit-foreign.ts findMasterWorkspace stops at the first ancestor with a `.git` entry, including a linked worktree's `.git` file. With Orca's workspaceDir `.orca/worktrees` (nested in the repo), `Repo: ../api` resolves to `<main>/.orca/worktrees/api` instead of the sibling of the main checkout. The prose pre-flight ('against this repo's root') has the same ambiguity. This matches the plan as written ('relative to the master's workspace'), so it is not a deviation, but a teammate running the audit in the main checkout and a coordinator in a worktree get different answers.
issues.suggested_fix: Prefer related.json names or absolute paths in the spec-master-plan prose (it already suggests related.json), and note that a relative Repo: is resolved from the checkout the audit runs in. Optionally resolve it against the main checkout by reading the `.git` file's gitdir/commondir without spawning git.

issues.title: Two exported `resolveRepoDir` functions have different semantics
issues.description: src/orca/dispatch-worktree.ts exports resolveRepoDir(repo) (absolute + realpath + must exist → {dir} | Failure), re-exported by dispatch.ts. src/spec/master-audit-foreign.ts exports resolveRepoDir(repo, masterWorkspace) (absolute / related.json name / relative → string, no existence check). The same name with different contracts invites the wrong import later.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename one of them, e.g. `resolveOrcaRepoDir` in dispatch-worktree.ts or `resolveSeedRepo` in master-audit-foreign.ts.

issues.title: The audit does not report a Repo: that resolves to no existing directory
issues.description: src/spec/master-audit-foreign.ts: when `Repo:` resolves to nothing (a misspelled related.json name falls through to a relative path), a seed without Location is reported as 'not started' with no finding. With a relative Location the only message is 'does not resolve to a readable plan', which does not say that the repo itself is missing.
issues.suggested_fix: When existsSync(repo) is false, add a foreign-location-missing message (or a warning) that names the unresolved `Repo:` value.

suggestions.title: A relative Location after the merge may point at the wrong checkout
suggestions.detail: resolve(repo, location) assumes the merge landed in Repo's main checkout. worktree_sync merges in the checkout that holds the base branch, so the audit can raise a false foreign-location-missing. Document this, or keep the absolute `Merged in:` path in that case.

suggestions.title: A relative Repo: resolves from the nearest .git (a linked/Orca worktree root)
suggestions.detail: With `.orca/worktrees` nested in the repo, `../api` resolves differently from a worktree than from the main checkout. Prefer related.json names in the prose, or resolve against the main checkout via the gitdir in the `.git` file.

suggestions.title: Two exported resolveRepoDir functions with different contracts
suggestions.detail: Rename one of them to avoid importing the wrong one.

suggestions.title: No finding when Repo: does not exist
suggestions.detail: Name the unresolved Repo: value in the finding instead of a generic Location message.
